newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs pressured.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products--Gulf gasoline diffs pressured.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials slipped lower by late Monday as the buyers backed out of the market, forcing sellers to chase them lower.
Midcontinent gasoline differentials remained near steady by late day after dipping about 0.50 during the first half of the day, although New York Harbor markets sat largely unchanged on the day.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained 0.63 cent to settle at 58.03 cents a gallon and July heating oil gained 0.30 cent to end at 51.94 cents.
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline fell to 3.10 to 3.35 cents below the July NYMEX by the end of the day after changing hands at 3.00 and 3.10 cents under the July NYMEX, according to traders.
Few buyers emerged to compete for the prompt barrels, one market player said, which led to the weakness in the differentials.
Reformulated A1 gasoline mimicked the weakness in the conventional, though players said confirmed deals were difficult to find. Prompt barrels were talked at about 1.50 cents under the July NYMEX.
Midcontinent markets were unchanged in afternoon trade, after losing about a half cent amid light selling earlier Monday.

"There are just more sellers than buyers," said one Group Three products trader. Prompt unleaded gasoline differentials in the hub held at 4.50/4.75 cents over July NYMEX. Any month offers were pegged at 3.25 cents.
Chicago unleaded differentials were 3.50/3.75 cents with any months at 2.25/3.00 cents. A 2.50-cent deal was heard done for any month barrels.
Little movement was noted by the end of the day, though prompt low sulphur diesel changed hands at 0.70 cent over the July NYMEX heating oil, the high end of the range seen Friday, traders said.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline differentials remained near steady between 2.50 and 2.75 cents under the July NYMEX, while reformulated A1 gasoline was pegged near 0.35 cent under.
